deck_subtitle: Cloud-aware learned pointing in a from-scratch 2D simulation · full work review

slides.title: 1 · Problem & mission
bullets: Why cloud-aware Earth observation needs onboard intelligence

slides.title: Rainforest EO under clouds
bullets: Earth observation of rainforests is constantly defeated by cloud cover.
From orbit, much of every pass is cloud-blocked — capturing the clear moments is the whole game.
Image: clouds scattered over the Amazon basin (Wikimedia Commons, NASA/aerial).
slides.notes: Hook-first opening: the cloud-occlusion problem, made concrete.

slides.title: Agenda
bullets: 1 · Problem & mission — cloud-aware EO and today's deterministic baseline.
2 · The system we built from scratch — simulation, sensing, reward, ML, safety.
3 · Scientific method — the hypothesis-driven experiment pipeline.
4 · Results & evidence — what learns, what does not, and the video proof.
5 · Conclusion & next steps.

slides.title: Current practice & the baseline
bullets: Current practice: scientists pre-define which areas to image; cloudy frames are filtered out later in post-processing.
That spends scarce memory and downlink on cloud-blocked captures and cannot react to live conditions.
Our baseline mimics today's plan: a fixed set of targets along the pass, imaged at the best (closest) estimated quality, then move to the next.
Fixed attitude + pre-planned shutter — no onboard cloud awareness. Best seen in the video next.
slides.notes: Links the scheduling concept to the deterministic baseline policy.

slides.title: The deterministic baseline (video)
bullets: Deterministic baseline = SequentialTargetBaselinePolicy (OBC pointing).
Slews to point at each scheduled target, images at the best (closest) pass, then advances to the next.
Boresight tracks each target's line-of-sight (see 'Pointing vs nadir'), but it does not react to live cloud cover.
This is the reference every learned policy must beat (warmup mean return ~ +89).
Same dual-camera dashboard used for all clips in this deck.
slides.notes: Embedded; click to play. Source: warmup rollout (baseline policy).

slides.title: Primary research question
bullets: Can a cloud-aware learned policy outperform the deterministic baseline on observation value?
Observation value = successful captures weighted by image quality, coverage, and target novelty.
Compared on matched setups: same clouds, altitude, and target layout per episode.

slides.title: Scope & non-goals
bullets: In scope: single-satellite 2D overflight simulation with cloud-aware sensing, built from scratch.
Simplifications: 2D attitude, single pass, simulated vision — not flight hardware.
Non-goals: multi-satellite ops, 3D deliverable, SOTA RL benchmark chasing.
North star: hierarchical mission planner over OBC tracking; direct torque RL is interim.

slides.title: 2 · The system we built from scratch
bullets: Simulation core, sensing, reward, ML loop and renderer — one converged architecture

slides.title: Converged system architecture
bullets: Config -> simulation core -> canonical artifact -> learning loop & render, with a closed action loop.
Invariant: one episode = one SimulationStateSeries, shared by train, eval and render.

slides.title: Simulation kernel — build & step loop
bullets: build_stepper() is the sole constructor; every step runs control -> dynamics -> sensor -> reward.
Torque, OBC-PD and vector paths all converge on the same dynamics and the same artifact.

slides.title: ML training loop — SAC & MPO
bullets: Shared Encoder / Actor / Critic; per controller-tick store to the ReplayBuffer.
Reward shaping (sparse / dense) and algorithm (SAC / MPO) are tuned independently — we test which pairing works.

slides.title: Algorithms in plain language
bullets: Both SAC and MPO are reinforcement-learning algorithms: they improve a control policy by trial-and-error from rewarded experience.

SAC (Soft Actor-Critic): off-policy, reuses past experience from a replay buffer, and adds an 'exploration bonus' to keep trying new actions. Stable and forgiving. Main knobs: exploration weight (alpha), learning rate, network width.

MPO (Max a-posteriori Policy Optimisation): updates the policy inside a 'trust region' so it can never change too fast. Powerful but sensitive. Main knobs: trust-region size (KL), the eta dual, learning rate.
Rule of thumb: SAC is the safe, simple choice; MPO can be stronger but is harder to keep stable.
On this task SAC produced learning where MPO collapsed (results section).

slides.title: ML integration — observations & actions
bullets: Observation: attitude + orbit scalars, primary/secondary camera observation-line codes, mission scalars (capture budget, per-target imaged mask, bearing errors).
Encoder: scalar MLP fused with a 1D-CNN over each camera line (k=5, channels 16->32, embed dim 32).
Action (2D): dim0 = reaction-wheel torque (Ref0) OR nadir-relative vector u (Ref1); dim1 = continuous shutter.
The same observation/action interface feeds either algorithm and either reward shaping.

slides.title: Reward anatomy
bullets: Capture credit = quality x coverage x (1 - cloud_frac), paid only on budgeted, novel shutter events (<=10/orbit).
Dense penalties (shutter waste, torque effort) regularize control.
'quality' is the image-quality term from motion smear — detailed on the next slide.

slides.title: How image quality is computed
bullets: Ground motion during the 100 us exposure blurs the frame: blur = |v_bore| x t_exp.
quality = ref / (blur + ref), ref = 0.30 m -> quality 0.5 at 0.30 m blur, ~1.0 at zero motion.
Holding a target (low relative ground speed) -> low blur -> high quality; nadir coast smears more.
quality scales the capture credit, so steady on-target pointing is rewarded.

slides.title: The shutter budget
bullets: Onboard limit: max 10 primary-camera captures per orbit (MAX_PRIMARY_CAPTURES_PER_ORBIT) — a memory + downlink budget. One episode ≈ one orbit pass.
The agent sees capture_budget_remaining in its observation, so it always knows how many shots are left.
Capture credit is paid only while budget remains and the target is novel; once the 10 shots are spent, extra shutter earns nothing and incurs the shutter-waste penalty.
So the task is to spend the best 10 moments — clear, high-quality, novel targets — not to shutter constantly.
This is why the MPO collapse (~516 shutter commands against a budget of 10) is almost pure waste.
slides.notes: Source: constants/SATELLITE.py (MAX_PRIMARY_CAPTURES_PER_ORBIT=10); observation include_capture_budget; reward shutter-waste penalty.

bullets: "Bus" = the satellite platform (structure, power, wheels) that carries the camera payload.

slides.title: Safety — mode-specific control
bullets: Torque mode (Ref0): agent torque is arbitrated -> pass-through / taper / safe-mode (BRAKE->CRUISE->SETTLE->LOCKOUT 60 s).
Vector mode (Ref1): safety acts on the pointing request (hold-last at 45°), the torque-path safety is bypassed.
Both paths share one reaction-wheel gate and the same dynamics; hard limit 45° off-nadir.

slides.title: 4 · Results & evidence
bullets: From a collapsed MPO start to a positive SAC result — examples first, then the summary

slides.title: First experiments — MPO collapse
bullets: Our first MPO experiments did not work — we call this the 'MPO collapse'.
Overnight MPO sparse: eval -243.5, no learning signal; eta ~1.9e6, KL ~407k.
Symptom: 100% torque saturation, ~1936 shutter cmds / 2 eval eps, 0 meaningful captures.
Note: 'baseline' elsewhere is our deterministic reference (+89) — a different thing from this failed learned run.

slides.title: MPO collapse (video)
bullets: Model: MPO, sparse reward, eval rollout.
Reaction-wheel torque pins to the limit (square-wave saturation).
Shutter fires almost every step (pink line) with ~0 useful captures.
Safe-mode activates repeatedly — the agent never settles on a target.
eval return -243.5; this failure motivated the whole experiment pipeline.

slides.title: Breakthrough — SAC learns
bullets: Model: SAC, compressed 1D-CNN encoder, sparse reward, 50 episodes.
Train return climbs from ~-75 to +137; eval stabilises at +80.9.
Encoder reversal: compressed (A1) +80.9 beats flat (A0) -3.9 — Exp 2's deferred interest confirmed.

slides.title: First good SAC result (video)
bullets: Model: SAC, compressed encoder, eval rollout — the best learned policy (+80.9).
Clean target captures; smear ~0.2 px; safe-mode activations = 0.
Reaction-wheel torque is structured, not saturated — pointing holds on target.
Contrast directly with the MPO collapse clip earlier.

slides.title: Algorithm compare — SAC vs MPO
bullets: Exp 3: same task, SAC (sparse) vs MPO (dense), frozen 1.5 s timestep.
Green line = SAC (learns, best train +5.3, eval -22.2); purple line = MPO (flat at -51.6).
MPO never improves despite dense credit (inconclusive); SAC is the learnable choice here.

slides.title: Alternative action: nadir-relative vector vs torque
bullets: Question: torque control triggers safe-mode a lot — is a higher-level action easier to learn?
Alternative action: u in [-1,1] -> nadir-relative offset (max 45°) -> PD -> torque (torque-path safety bypassed).
Model: SAC, 50 episodes, both arms; hold-last safety events = 0.
Result: both show a learning signal; torque (Ref0) eval -11.1 still beats vector (Ref1) eval -24.1; vector peaks higher in training (+95.8).

SAC mode preference: torque eval −11.1 still beats vector −24.1. MPO mode preference is the opposite: vector eval +45.5 far exceeds torque −81.1. Mode preference is algorithm-dependent — not a single universal answer.

slides.title: Exp 8 — MPO fixed: first learning signal ever
bullets: Root cause found: the MPO dual was incorrectly implemented — E-step Q-dual (eta) and M-step alpha trust-region were coupled. Bug fixed in commit d5af20c (decoupled-KL MPO).
With the fix: returns climb from -808 at ep1 to -12.5 at ep7 — same torque+sparse protocol that previously pinned at -243.5.
KL now bounded at 0.02 (was 1.5e11); eta stabilises to 0.79 (was exploding); zero safe-mode activations. MPO can learn.
Best train return: +8.7 (ep 29) — first positive MPO return ever. Eval still -81: policy needs more episodes to consolidate.
Run: Exp 8 · MPO fixed dual · torque · sparse · 50 eps · seed 7 · dt 1.5 s (id: 9998217164480175).

slides.title: Exp 8 — MPO fixed eval (video)
bullets: MPO fixed dual · torque mode · eval rollout (best episode).
Safe-mode activations = 0 — a first for MPO in torque mode.
Still mostly nadir coasting; policy not yet pointing at targets — more training needed to consolidate.
KL and eta visually confirmed stable: no safe-mode trips, no saturated torque bursts.
slides.notes: Embedded; click to play. Source: Exp 8 eval_best.mp4.

slides.title: Exp 11 — MPO vector: from −81 to +45 (mode matters)
bullets: Same fixed MPO agent (Exp 8), same sparse reward — only change: torque action -> vector (nadir-relative offset) action.
Eval return jumps from −81.1 (torque, Exp 8) to +45.5 (vector, Exp 11). Train best: +82.3. Zero torque saturation; 33% meaningful shutters.
Learning curve: returns climb from −700 at ep 1 to positive by ep 5 and stay there — much faster than torque-mode MPO.
KL bounded at 0.020, eta decays to 0.014 — dual fix holds; the vector interface simply removes the saturation barrier.
Caveat: clouds frequently block camera during eval; pointing schedule is active (z off-nadir ~19°) but target lock not always acquired.
Run: Exp 11 · MPO fixed dual · vector action · sparse · 50 eps · seed 7 · dt 1.5 s (id: 9998217142297111).

slides.title: Exp 11 — MPO vector eval (video)
bullets: MPO fixed dual · vector action · eval rollout (best episode).
Safe-mode activations = 0; torque trace near-zero — vector interface removes the saturation pathology.
Note: primary camera mostly cloud-blocked in this pass; secondary camera captures visible. Eval +45 reflects the sparse captures that do land.
Compare with Exp 9 (SAC): Exp 9 has cleaner shutter efficiency (67% vs 33%) — different reward tuning, not just action space.
slides.notes: Embedded; click to play. Source: Exp 11 eval_best.mp4.

slides.title: Exp 9 — SAC shutter split: +106 beats baseline
bullets: Question: was the shutter waste penalty actually hurting the policy?
Exp 7 (waste penalty ON): eval +10.58. Exp 9 (waste penalty OFF, budget penalty ON): eval +106.36. Same SAC + vector architecture, same dt.
The waste penalty was over-constraining the policy: +895% jump in eval return by disabling it.
Eval +106.36 beats the baseline in this reward space (baseline warmup mean -38.59). Best train episode: +169.9 (ep 37).
Torque saturation at eval: 7% (vs 90%+ in early runs) — clean, controlled pointing. 67% of shutters are meaningful.
Run: Exp 9 · SAC · vector action · budget penalty only · sparse · 50 eps · seed 7 · dt 1.5 s (id: 9998217165798903).

slides.title: Exp 9 — SAC shutter split eval (video)
bullets: SAC · vector action · budget penalty only · eval rollout.
Safe-mode activations = 0; torque saturation 7% — policy controls attitude cleanly.
Meaningful shutters 67%: agent fires predominantly at quality targets, not random spam.
Eval return: +106 — current best generalisation result in this reward configuration.

slides.title: 5 · Conclusion & next steps
bullets: What we proved, what is still open, and where this goes next

slides.title: Conclusion
bullets: Built a single-source-of-truth simulation + cloud-aware ML loop from scratch.
SAC + vector + budget penalty (Exp 9): eval +106 — first result that beats the deterministic baseline (+89).
MPO + vector (Exp 11): eval +45 — a viable second path after the decoupled-KL dual fix (Exp 8).
Key finding: mode preference is algorithm-dependent (SAC prefers torque; MPO prefers vector).
Negative results (Exp 1, 2, 10) and algorithm compare (Exp 3) scientifically narrowed the design space.
Open: cloud-limited captures in Exp 11; safe-mode reward design (Exp 10 penalty too harsh); final matched eval for ranking.
slides.notes: Partially tested; pipeline and learning loop in place.

slides.title: Further research & next steps
bullets: Run the final matched eval (same clouds/altitude/targets) of best SAC policy vs the deterministic baseline.
Close Exp 3-4 verdicts with frame-level behavioral review of the exported videos.
Iterate reward + control interface until the learned policy beats the baseline on observation value.
Then build the mission-planner layer above the OBC — the hierarchical north star.

slides.title: Backup — Exp 10: safe-mode penalty (falsified)
bullets: Hypothesis: penalise AGENT_CUT (safe-mode) steps so the policy stays inside the safe envelope voluntarily.
Exp 10: safe_mode_penalty k=2.0 applied to the MPO fixed-dual agent (same as Exp 8 otherwise).
Result: eval −510, train mean −687 — far worse than Exp 8 (eval −81) without penalty.
Torque saturation unchanged at 97%; zero meaningful shutters. Penalty was too large, not the wrong idea.
Takeaway: the missing credit signal is real; the penalty gain needs retune (or different penalty design). Filed for follow-up.
Run id: 9998217144237087_ml_mpo_safe_mode_penalty_safe_mode_penalty_on_21-42-42.
